hints: The resistance is given by $R = kv^2$.
Substitute $R = 480\text{ N}$ and speed $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$ into this formula.
Divide 480 by $24^2 = 576$ and simplify to a fraction in lowest terms.
walkthrough:
Use the resistance law $R = kv^2$ with $R = 480\text{ N}$ and $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$480 = k(24^2)$$
$$480 = 576k$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the given resistance formula:
$$R = kv^2$$

Substitute the given numerical values when the speed is $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and the resistance is $480\text{ N}$:
$$480 = k \times 24^2$$

Divide both sides by 576:
$$k = \frac{480}{576}$$

Divide the numerator and denominator by 96:
$$480 = 5 \times 96,\quad 576 = 6 \times 96 \implies k = \frac{5}{6}$$
Hence, the constant is $k = \frac{5}{6}$.

hints: The car moves up the slope at a constant speed, so acceleration is zero ($a = 0$).
Equate the driving force to the sum of the resistance force and the downhill component of weight: $F_D = R + mg\sin\alpha$.
Substitute $R = 480\text{ N}$, $m = 1400\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\sin\alpha = 0.12$.
Once $F_D$ is found, calculate the engine power using $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces parallel to the incline for motion at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - R - mg\sin\alpha = 0$$
$$F_D = R + mg\sin\alpha$$

Calculate the power of the engine using $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 2160 \times 24 = 51840\text{ W}\quad (51.84\text{ kW})$$
teacher_walkthrough: The car travels uphill at a constant speed of $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Since the speed is constant, the acceleration along the slope is zero ($a = 0$).
Apply equilibrium of forces along the line of greatest slope:

The forces acting down the slope are the resistance force $R = 480\text{ N}$ and the component of gravity down the slope $mg\sin\alpha$. The forward driving force is $F_D$:
$$F_D = R + mg\sin\alpha$$

Substitute the values $m = 1400\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\sin\alpha = 0.12$:
$$mg\sin\alpha = 1400 \times 10 \times 0.12 = 14000 \times 0.12 = 1680\text{ N}$$

Add the resistance force:
$$F_D = 480 + 1680 = 2160\text{ N}$$

Now state the power formula relating driving force and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute $F_D = 2160\text{ N}$ and $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 2160 \times 24$$

Perform the multiplication:
$$2160 \times 20 = 43200$$
$$2160 \times 4 = 8640$$
$$P = 43200 + 8640 = 51840\text{ W}$$
Thus, the power of the car engine is $51840\text{ W}$ (or $51.8\text{ kW}$).

hints: On a level road at constant speed, the driving force balances the resistance force: $F_D = R = kv^2$, with $k = \frac{5}{6}$.
Use the relation $P = F_D \times v$ with power $54\text{ kW} = 54000\text{ W}$.
Substitute $F_D = \frac{5}{6}v^2$ into $P = F_D v$ to obtain a cubic equation in $v$: $\frac{5}{6}v^3 = 54000$, and solve for $v$.
walkthrough:
Equate driving force to resistance for constant speed on a level road:
$$F_D = kv^2 = \frac{5}{6}v^2$$

Use the power formula $P = F_D \times v$ with $P = 54\text{ kW} = 54000\text{ W}$:
$$\left(\frac{5}{6}v^2\right)v = 54000$$
$$\frac{5}{6}v^3 = 54000$$
teacher_walkthrough: From part (a)(i), the constant in the resistance law $R = kv^2$ is $k = \frac{5}{6}$.

The car travels at constant speed on a level horizontal road. Since there is no acceleration ($a = 0$) and no slope, the driving force $F_D$ must exactly balance the air resistance:
$$F_D = R = kv^2 = \frac{5}{6}v^2$$

Recall the relationship connecting engine power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute $F_D = \frac{5}{6}v^2$ into the power formula:
$$P = \left(\frac{5}{6}v^2\right)v = \frac{5}{6}v^3$$

The engine power is given as $54\text{ kW} = 54000\text{ W}$:
$$\frac{5}{6}v^3 = 54000$$

Multiply both sides by 6 and divide by 5:
$$v^3 = \frac{54000 \times 6}{5} = 10800 \times 6 = 64800$$

Take the cube root to find the constant speed $v$:
$$v = \sqrt[3]{64800} \approx 40.16599 \approx 40.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus, the constant speed of the car on the level road is $40.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Forms $\frac{5}{6}v^3 = 54000$ and solves for $v = (64800)^{1/3} \approx 40.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
